newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa hopes EU will lift ostrich ban next week.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa hopes EU will lift ostrich ban next week.

text.p: South African ostrich meat exporters said on Wednesday they hoped the European Union would lift its ban on imports next week.

The chairman of the South African National Ostrich Processors Association, Peter Strydom, said in a telephone interview that research into whether the meat is safe for human consumption should be completed by Saturday.

The EU recommended that members bar ostrich meat imports from South Africa, which dominates the world market, after an outbreak of Congo-Crimean haemorrhagic fever among workers at the country's biggest ostrich abattoir last month.

Strydom said South African research into ostrich meat, being overseen by an EU veterinarian, was sure to declare it safe. The findings would be presented to EU veterinary officials who he said would meet in Brussels on Tuesday.
"We hope it will go well on Tuesday...I'm sure by Wednesday we'll be able to start the meat going into Europe again," Strydom said.
Researchers say the ill abattoir workers, one of whom died, could have contracted the disease from ticks carried by slaughter birds.
Strydom said producers had not lost money because meat from slaughtered birds had been frozen. South Africa exports about 16 million tonnes of ostrich meat a year, 85 percent of it to Europe.
Strydom said Asian markets such as Hong Kong, China, Singapore, Malaysia and Japan were still importing ostrich meat from South Africa.
